evals.name: double-booking
evals.prompt: Two customers keep booking the last room of the same type at the same time and we oversell beyond our 10% overbooking allowance. Reservation traffic is only ~3 TPS. Fix the data model and the concurrency.
evals.expected_output: Room-type inventory table keyed by (hotel_id, room_type_id, date) with total_inventory and total_reserved, availability check against 110%, idempotency key with a unique constraint for double clicks, optimistic locking or a CHECK constraint (not pessimistic) given low contention, citing Vol. 2 ch. 7.
expectations: Proposes the room_type_inventory table with total_inventory and total_reserved per date.
Uses an idempotency key (reservation_id) with a unique constraint for the same-user double click.
Recommends optimistic locking or a database CHECK constraint and explains why pessimistic locking is not preferred.
States the overbooking check as total_reserved + n <= 110% of total_inventory.
Cites Vol. 2 ch. 7 (or chapter 22 in the upstream numbering).

evals.name: wallet-transfer-atomicity
evals.prompt: Our wallet balances are sharded across 20 Postgres nodes. A transfer debits on one shard and credits on another. How do we make it atomic at 1M TPS and auditable?
evals.expected_output: Reject 2PC (locks, coordinator SPOF); Try-Confirm/Cancel with a phase status table and deduct-before-add ordering, or an orchestrated Saga; event sourcing with a deterministic state machine, local append-only log, Raft-replicated events, snapshots, CQRS reads, citing Vol. 2 ch. 12.
expectations: Explains why two-phase commit is a poor fit (lock contention, coordinator as single point of failure).
Describes Try-Confirm/Cancel or an orchestrated Saga with compensating transactions and a phase status table.
Recommends event sourcing for auditability and replay, with a deterministic state machine.
Mentions Raft replication of the event log (only the events need high reliability).
Cites Vol. 2 ch. 12 (or chapter 27 in the upstream numbering).
